findings.title: `authConditions` is always truthy, so two branches in `getBaseConditions` are unreachable
findings.description: `getAuthorizationConditions()` is typed `Promise<Prisma.Sql>` and always returns a `Sql` object, never `null`. The checks `if (authConditions && filterConditions)` and `else if (authConditions)` therefore reduce to `if (filterConditions)` and an unconditional return. The `else if (filterConditions)` branch and the final `else` returning `NOTHING_CONDITION` can never run. The results are still correct, because an always-present auth condition is combined with the filter, and `NOTHING_CONDITION` is applied inside the auth result. The problem is that the code reads as if auth can be absent, which misleads future maintainers. The old code filtered with `c !== null` against a nullable type, so this is a new mismatch introduced by the rewrite. Either drop the dead branches or make the nullability of `authConditions` match the code.
